characterization_methods.key_findings: 4Al variant weakly affected by aging; see property_set prop_mech_1.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state

characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness nearly flat around 200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al (4Al included).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane; samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations; as-cast coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling + water quenching produced a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grains and some retained Mn microsegregations.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sections perpendicular to the rolling direction prepared by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure investigation (cracks, pores, macrosegregations, grain structure)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: The 4 wt.% Al variant is only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of mechanical data, compared with Fe-30Mn-1.2C (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace; successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130 mm³ blocks hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments with dimensions 2×60×55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All values plotted represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic microstructure with a grain size of ~20 μm and some retained Mn microsegregations; a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature for Al content below 5 wt.%.

unmapped_findings: The paper does not report a discrete 500 °C/24 h data point specifically for the 4 wt.% Al alloy; the mechanical values available for 4Al are aggregated across aging conditions in Fig. 3 and Fig. 4.

b0025: The intermediate alloy variants with 2–6 wt.% Al do not show equivalent mechanical properties compared to the ~8 wt.% Al variant, and show a much smaller influence of aging on the tensile behavior.

b0031: For compositions with 25–30 wt.% Mn and up to 4–5 wt.% Al (SIMPLEX steels) the TWIP effect prevails as the deformation mechanism; after aging at 500–600 °C twinning is reduced and strain hardening becomes associated with κ-carbide and solid-solution strengthening (relevant to this 4Al/500 °C aged sample).
No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations were found in the final RAP materials (b0021), and the 4 wt.% Al variant is reported as an intermediate variant between the 0Al and 8Al aging responses (b0024).
